one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled catalyst falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30. Q3 FY27 results come in early December (the fiscal quarter ends Oct 31). The CEO exit (8-K Sep 28, stock -18%) and the Investor Day (Sep 29, targets raised, Q3/FY27 guidance reaffirmed) are already in the $356 close. So is the Sep 30 PCE print, which the supervisor reports cut October hike odds to about 36%. Events inside the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, late-October hyperscaler cloud results (a read-across for Atlas consumption), and unscheduled CEO-search news, which could cut either way. Support comes from the $1.35B remaining buyback (Sep 25 8-K) and the partial rebound already under way ($335 to $356). Net: close to symmetric, median about $357, monthly sigma about 16.5%. That is a bit below the 71%/3.5 rule because two one-off event gaps inflate the realized figure and no comparable event is scheduled. This is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Equal blend of forward P/E and EV/NTM-sales at Sep-2027, with one share count (85M fully diluted) throughout. P/E: NTM non-GAAP EPS of about $10.05 (1/3 FY28 $8.43 + 2/3 FY29 $10.87) x 38 = $382. EV/sales: NTM revenue of about $4.12B x 7.5 = $30.9B, plus about $2.6B net cash, divided by 85M = $394. Blend about $388.

bear.story: The March 2027 FY28 guide comes in at about 15-17% growth (the guide-implied Q4 of about +14% sets the tone), Atlas slides toward 20%, the CEO search drags on or go-to-market leaders leave, and Postgres/DocumentDB pressure caps the multiple. About 5x NTM sales gives about $225.

base.story: MDB beats the H2 guide modestly, guides FY28 at about 18-19% and grows about 20%, Atlas stays in the mid-20s, margins expand about 150 bps a year, and a permanent CEO is named within 6-9 months. About 38x NTM EPS / 7.5x sales.

bull.story: AI workloads (vector search, Voyage, Agent Engine) keep Atlas at 27%+, MDB keeps beating by about 5%, the FY28 guide lands at 20%+, and a strong CEO hire restores the premium. About 10x sales / 50x EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Around $240 (-33%), about 5.5x NTM EV/sales on about $4.1B and back in the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone. Getting there without a broad market crash would most likely mean the March 2027 FY28 guide fell well below about 18%, Atlas growth slid toward 20% or below, or senior go-to-market leaders left during the CEO search. That would break the Investor Day 20%+ framework, not just add event noise; the business grew 30% with 122% net ARR expansion as of Q2.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my round-1 inputs (NTM weighting, about $10 EPS, buyback detail) and flagged two points, which I checked in the primary releases. (1) Share count: I now use 85M fully diluted in both legs; the EV/sales leg falls from $405 to $394. (2) Q4 implication: the Q1 FY27 release shows revenue of $687.6M and a Q2 guide of $729-734M; the Q2 release shows $771.8M (a 5.1% beat) and the FY guide raised to $2.99-3.03B. So H1 = $1,459.4M and implied Q4 = about $775-810M, about +14% at the midpoint against $695.1M (Q4 FY26, +27%). Part of Q2's beat was EA term-license lumpiness (EA +36% vs +13% in Q1), so I assume only about a 2% H2 beat, put FY27 at about $3.05B and shade FY28 growth to 19%. The P/E leg: NTM EPS about $10.05 x 38 = $382. The EV/sales leg: $4.12B x 7.5 + $2.6B cash on 85M shares = $394. The blend is $388 (from $395). I agree with the supervisor on nearly everything. Its $9.9 EPS is a touch below my $10.05 because I start from a modestly beaten FY27, and I keep that. For the March FY28 guide as a downside event, I raise the bear probability to 27% and lower the bear price to $225. Scenario mean is about $380; median about $368 after leadership-transition drag. Ladder: lognormal, median about $368, sigma 0.50 (below the 71% realized, which two event gaps inflated), with slightly fatter far tails. P(>=356) = 0.527, from 0.54. The 1-month ladder is essentially unchanged: no company event in the window, so it is near-symmetric with a median of about $357.
